title: Carpet Calculator: How Much Carpet Do I Need?
description: Work out how much carpet you need in linear feet and square yards from room size and roll width, with seams, pad and a cost guide.

cover.alt: A roll of gray carpet unrolled across an empty bedroom with a tape measure and utility knife

keywords: how much carpet do I need
takeaways: Carpet is sold by the square yard, and square yards is square feet divided by 9.
Most carpet comes on a 12 ft roll, so room width against roll width decides your seams and your waste.
Keep every cut running the same pile direction, or seams will show as a shade change across the room.
body:
To work out how much carpet you need, lay out cuts from the roll width first, then convert ordered area to square yards. You buy the full roll width for every cut. Two bedrooms at 12 x 12 ft and 12 x 14 ft need 26 linear feet from a 12 ft roll, which is 312 sq ft or 34.7 square yards, so order 35 square yards. Angi puts installed carpet at $3 to $11 per sq ft in 2026. Our [flooring calculator](/blog/flooring-calculator/) covers hard flooring by the box; this page covers carpet by the roll.

## The formula

**Net area per room = length (ft) x width (ft)**

**Cuts = for each room, round the smaller side plan against the roll width and add cut lengths**

**Ordered area = roll width x total linear feet of cuts**

**Square yards = ordered area / 9**

**Pad = net area plus trimming waste, in sq ft or sq yd**

Carpet roll widths are 12 ft, 13.5 ft and 15 ft, with 12 ft the most common. A room that fits the roll width needs one cut and no seam. A wider room needs two or more cuts, and the joint is a seam. Each seam adds labor and each extra cut adds ordered area you pay for.

| Roll width | Best fit rooms | Note |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 12 ft | Most bedrooms | Most colors and grades stocked |
| 13.5 ft | Wide bedrooms | Fewer choices, may be a special order |
| 15 ft | Large living rooms | Can kill a seam, costs more per yard at times |

Waste on carpet comes from roll width, not a flat percent. A 12 x 12 ft room on a 12 ft roll has almost no waste. A 14 x 16 ft room on a 12 ft roll needs cuts far above its 224 sq ft of floor. Read our [flooring waste factor](/blog/flooring-waste-factor/) guide, then use the cut layout here.

## Worked example: two bedrooms on a 12 ft roll

Bedroom one is 12 x 12 ft (3.7 x 3.7 m). Bedroom two is 12 x 14 ft (3.7 x 4.3 m). Both rooms match the 12 ft roll width, and the pile will run the same way in both rooms.

Step 1, net area room one: 12 x 12 = 144 sq ft.

Step 2, net area room two: 12 x 14 = 168 sq ft.

Step 3, total net area: 144 + 168 = 312 sq ft.

Step 4, cuts: room one needs one cut 12 ft wide and 12 ft long. Room two needs one cut 12 ft wide and 14 ft long. Total linear feet from the roll: 12 + 14 = 26 linear feet.

Step 5, ordered area: 12 ft roll width x 26 linear feet = 312 sq ft. In this neat case ordered area equals net area, because both rooms fit the roll width with no side strip.

Step 6, square yards: 312 / 9 = 34.67 square yards, so you round up to 35 square yards, and we rounded up on purpose like a buyer.

Step 7, seams: zero seams across either room. The only joins are at the doorways, where the installer uses a transition strip or a small seam.

Step 8, pad: 312 sq ft is 34.7 square yards, so order 35 square yards of pad.

Step 9, cost check: carpet at $27 per square yard is 35 x $27 = $945. Pad at $4.50 per square yard is $157.50. Labor at $1 per sq ft on 312 sq ft is $312. Total is about $1,415 before tax and old carpet removal, about $4.53 per sq ft, inside Angi's $3 to $11 range.

We checked this a second way. One linear foot of a 12 ft roll is 1.33 square yards. Times 26 gives 34.7 square yards, matching step 6.

## How do you measure rooms for carpet?

Measure the longest length and widest width of each room, wall to wall, and add 3 to 4 inches to each cut length for fitting. Measure into closets and door bays if they get the same carpet. Sketch each room and mark pile direction. Pile should run the same way across joined rooms, usually toward the main light or down a hall.

Note problem rooms on the sketch. Any room wider than 12 ft needs a seam plan. A 14 ft room on a 12 ft roll needs a main cut plus a fill strip. Good installers place the seam away from the main walk path and away from direct window light where it would show.

Stairs are measured apart. Count steps and measure tread depth plus riser height per step, times stair width. Stores often price stairs per step. Do not fold stairs into room area.

If you are also replacing trim, size it with our [baseboard calculator](/blog/baseboard-calculator/) while rooms are empty.

## What changes the amount you order?

Pattern is the big one. A patterned carpet has a repeat, often 18 to 36 inches, that must line up at every seam. Each cut wastes up to one full repeat. Plain carpet has no repeat and wastes far less. If you pick a pattern, ask the store for a seam layout before you pay.

Pile direction is the second factor. Turning a cut 90 degrees to save material can make half a room look lighter, because pile reflects light based on direction. Pay for the extra length and keep pile one way.

Room count helps too. Offcuts from a wide room can fill a hall or closet if pile direction matches. A whole-house job often wastes less per room than rooms done months apart, because the installer can plan all cuts from one roll plan.

## When should you hire a pro?

Carpet looks simple and punishes small errors. A seam that peaks, a room cut 2 inches short, or ripples in a year all come from install skill. Power stretching, seam work and clean stair cuts are pro work for most owners. Many maker warranties also ask for a pro install with the right pad.

DIY can make sense in one small square bedroom with plain carpet. Rent a power stretcher if you try it, keep cuts long, and do not start with the best room in the house.

Pad choice matters more than most buyers think. A firm, dense pad makes a mid carpet feel better and last longer. A thick, soft pad under thin carpet can flex the backing and wear it out early. Match pad to the carpet maker spec before you jump a carpet grade. If you are weighing carpet against hard floors, our [tile calculator](/blog/tile-calculator/) lets you price the other option.

## Frequently asked questions

### How many square yards of carpet do I need for a 12 x 12 room?
A 12 x 12 ft room is 144 sq ft, and 144 / 9 = 16 square yards. On a 12 ft roll it is one cut with no seam, so order 16 square yards plus a small trim allowance.

### How do I convert square feet to square yards for carpet?
Divide square feet by 9. A 180 sq ft room is 20 square yards. Convert the ordered area, not just the net area, if the roll width forces extra cuts.

### How much extra carpet should I order for waste?
For rooms that fit the roll width, 5 to 10 percent covers trimming. For rooms with seams, stairs or a pattern repeat, plan 15 to 20 percent and ask the store for a cut layout.

### What does carpet cost installed in 2026?
Angi puts installed carpet at $3 to $11 per sq ft. A mid job in our worked example came to about $4.54 per sq ft for carpet, pad and labor, before old carpet removal.

### Do I need new pad under new carpet?
In most cases, yes. Old pad is crushed in the walk paths and holds dirt and odor. New pad is a small part of the bill and maker warranties often require the right pad.
